H1.text: Someone who is sixteen point nine years old says their age is sixteen. Not seventeen.

H2.text: Age counts completed years. Sixteen point one, sixteen point five, sixteen point nine: all just sixteen.

H3.text: Diya saw this on the health camp form at college.

H4.text: Rounding down looks easy. But what is minus two point one, rounded down? Minus two, or minus three?

H5.text: Two special functions answer this. Signum, and the greatest integer function.

S1.text: First, signum, the Latin word for sign.

S2.text: It asks one thing. Is a number positive, negative, or zero?

S3.text: Positive x gives one. Zero gives zero. Negative x gives minus one.

S4.text: Watch x slide. Minus three gives minus one. Minus a half, still minus one. Only the sign matters.

S5.text: At zero, the output is zero. Just after zero, it jumps to one, and stays there.

S6.text: Two flat rays and one dot at the origin. Domain: all real numbers. Range: just minus one, zero and one.

M1.text: NCERT also writes signum with the modulus. Mod x, over x.

M2.text: Step one. If x is five, mod x is five. Five over five is one.

M3.text: Step two. If x is minus five, mod x is still five. Five over minus five is minus one.

M4.text: Step three. At zero we cannot divide, so signum of zero is defined as zero.

G1.text: Now the greatest integer function. We write it as x inside square brackets.

G2.text: Square bracket x means the greatest integer that is less than or equal to x.

G3.text: List every integer not bigger than x, then pick the largest one.

G4.text: Take two point seven. The integers not bigger than it are two, one, zero, and so on. The largest is two.

G5.text: Now take exactly three. Three is allowed, so square bracket three is three.

K1.text: Careful. Chopping off the decimal is different. For two point seven, both give two.

K2.text: For minus two point one, chopping gives minus two. But minus two is to the right, so it is bigger.

K3.text: Your turn. Square bracket minus two point one. Minus two, or minus three? Pause and decide.

K4.text: Minus three! It is the first integer to the left. Rounding down always moves left.

T1.text: Remember this. The greatest integer function always rounds down, to the left.

D1.text: Now let x run, and draw the graph.

D2.text: From minus two up to minus one, square bracket x stays at minus two.

D3.text: Then it is zero, then one. Each value holds flat, then jumps.

D4.text: The graph is a staircase. A filled dot starts each step, and an empty dot ends it.

D5.text: Filled means that end is included. Empty means it is not.

D6.text: Step one. For x from zero up to one, but not one, square bracket x is zero.

D7.text: Step two. For x from one up to two, but not two, it is one.

D8.text: Step three. In general, if square bracket x is n, then n is less than or equal to x, and x is less than n plus one.

D9.text: The domain is all real numbers. The range is the integers.

Z1.text: Quick one. At x equal to two, is the staircase at height one, or two? Pause and think.

Z2.text: Height two! Square bracket two is two. The filled dot starts the new step.

W2.text: Solve two times square bracket x, minus one, equals five.

W3.text: Step one. Add one to both sides. Two times square bracket x is six.

W4.text: Step two. Divide by two. Square bracket x is three.

W5.text: Step three. The staircase rule. Three is less than or equal to x, and x is less than four.

W6.text: Step four. So x is any number from three, included, up to four, not included.

W7.text: A whole step of answers. Three point nine nine works. Four does not.

X2.text: Find square bracket minus three point seven. Many students drop the decimal: minus three.

X3.text: But minus three is bigger. Move left to the first integer. The answer is minus four.

J1.text: Where is it asked? JEE Main, in questions that build a function from square bracket x and ask for its range.

Q1.text: Exam level now. This function mixes both ideas. What is its range? Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is C. Minus two, minus one, zero and one.

A2.text: At x equal to zero, every part is zero.

A3.text: For any other integer, the two brackets cancel to zero. So f is just the sign, one or minus one.

A4.text: For a number that is not an integer, the two brackets add to minus one.

A5.text: So f is zero for positive x, and minus two for negative x. Range: minus two, minus one, zero, one.

Y2.text: One. What is the signum of minus seven? And the signum of zero?

Y3.text: Two. Find square bracket minus zero point five.

Y4.text: Three. For which numbers x is square bracket x equal to five?
